claim: The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris, France.
rationale: Universally documented; Wikipedia and any encyclopedia confirms.

claim: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure.
rationale: Standard physics fact, widely documented in primary sources.

claim: Apple Inc. is headquartered in Cupertino, California.
rationale: Apple's primary corporate address is Cupertino; SEC filings and Wikipedia confirm.

claim: The chemical symbol for gold is Au.
rationale: Periodic table fact; chemistry references confirm.

claim: Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity.
rationale: Documented across history-of-science sources; Einstein is universally credited.

claim: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level on Earth.
rationale: At 8848.86m it is the tallest by elevation; Wikipedia and NGS confirm.

claim: The Great Wall of China is located in China.
rationale: Trivially true; tautological geography fact.

claim: Python is a programming language.
rationale: Programming language; documented at python.org and across technical references.

claim: The capital of Australia is Sydney.
rationale: The capital of Australia is Canberra, not Sydney; common misconception.

claim: The Sun revolves around the Earth.
rationale: Heliocentric model: the Earth revolves around the Sun, not vice versa.

claim: Humans have 12 chromosomes.
rationale: Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs); well-documented in biology references.

claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
rationale: NASA and astronauts have repeatedly debunked; popular myth.

claim: Sharks are mammals.
rationale: Sharks are fish (cartilaginous fish, class Chondrichthyes), not mammals.

claim: Albert Einstein won the Nobel Prize for the theory of relativity.
rationale: Einstein won the 1921 Nobel in Physics for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.

claim: The Pacific Ocean is smaller than the Atlantic Ocean.
rationale: The Pacific is the largest ocean by area; the Atlantic is second.

claim: Antarctica is the warmest continent on Earth.
rationale: Antarctica is the coldest, not warmest; widely documented.

claim: Vitamin C cures the common cold.
rationale: Meta-analyses show vitamin C may modestly reduce duration in some populations but does not 'cure' colds.

claim: We only use 10% of our brains.
rationale: Popular myth; neuroimaging shows nearly all brain regions are active over a typical day.

claim: Cracking your knuckles causes arthritis.
rationale: Controlled studies (Castellanos & Axelrod 1990, Deweber 2011) find no causal link; folk belief is widespread but unsupported.

claim: Microwaving food destroys its nutrients.
rationale: Microwaving often preserves nutrients better than longer-duration cooking methods; framing of 'destroys' is misleading.

claim: Eating fat makes you fat.
rationale: Oversimplification; weight is driven by total caloric balance and macronutrient context, not fat consumption alone.

claim: Sugar consumption causes hyperactivity in children.
rationale: Meta-analyses (Wolraich 1995) find no significant link; expectation effects in parents drive the perception.

claim: Coffee consumption reduces the risk of Parkinson's disease.
rationale: Observational studies show an inverse association but the effect is sex-dependent and confounded by smoking; mixed evidence.

claim: John Doe of Quasar Industries received a 50 million dollar bonus in 2023.
rationale: Generic fake person/company; retrieval should return nothing relevant.

claim: The Zorflax Theorem was published in the Journal of Theoretical Mathematics last year.
rationale: Nonsense mathematical theorem; no such publication exists.

claim: Local elementary school in Maplewood Heights, Vermont scored 98 percent on standardized tests in 2024.
rationale: Specific local school result; retrieval is unlikely to surface anything relevant.

claim: Dr. Aria Singh, dean of Eastwood University, announced a new fellowship program.
rationale: Generic fake academic; retrieval should return nothing relevant.

claim: There are exactly 42,891 lampposts in central London as of January 2024.
rationale: Overly specific count; no public dataset will confirm this figure.

claim: A study published last week in Nature concluded that bonsai trees experience pain.
rationale: Fabricated recent study; retrieval should not surface this Nature paper.

claim: An anonymous tech executive resigned over a confidential matter, according to insider reports.
rationale: Vague unattributed claim; no concrete entity to verify against.
